speaker: Ms Joan Pereira
text: asked the Minister for Health in light of the IT glitch in the computer system of clinics where patients received mislabelled medicines (a) what corrective action has been taken to ensure that the IT system is robust and secure; and (b) what measures are being taken to prevent such future incidences.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong
text: asked the Minister for Health what led to over 100 clinics prescribing the wrong dosage for 800 patients and whether there were any adverse effects for the affected patients.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Several clinics were aware of the error and manually corrected the dosage instruction on the label.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: The vendor also did not report any errors from the other tests done.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Since the incident, additional rounds of testing have been conducted to ensure that existing functions within GP Connect are working as designed.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: The "Unit of Measurement" function is also being enhanced to prevent future errors.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: IHiS is also thoroughly reviewing testing procedures prior to future software rollouts to prevent such occurrences.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: In addition, they will step up monitoring of software rollouts and improve their response to better support users.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: First, would the Ministry consider putting in place a process encouraging doctors to print out a copy of the prescription for the patient after examination and going through with him the medicines and dosages?

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: The second one, could this same printout be given to the patient so that the dispenser can countercheck against the labels and instructions on the medicines?

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: In fact, variants of this practice are already being done in many clinics.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: When medications are dispensed in clinics, it is common practice for the doctors to advise patients at the point of prescribing, for example, alerting the patients to any dosage adjustments to their regular chronic medication.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: And it is also the responsibility of the clinic licensee and doctors to ensure that there is proper process of verifying the prescriptions during dispensing of the medicines to the patients.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: The Ministry of Health (MOH) will continue to work with practitioners as well as the professional medical bodies to improve patient safety and medication safety and minimise any possible medication dispensing errors in the future.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Would IHiS be held accountable for this error in any way?

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: I will leave it to IHiS to manage the situation with the respective IT vendor.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Would the Ministry be considering looking at new security measures or new technologies, such as block chain, for example, to ensure the security and immutability of the data so that such sensitive data, such as prescribed medicine, can be assured?

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: With regard to this particular incident, it is a human error whereby a wrong application code was applied.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Of course, we will put in place measures to ensure that such errors can be picked up early or even prevented right from the outset.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: As to Dr Intan Azura's suggestion of using new technology or block chain technology to enhance the security of such a system, MOH will seriously look into it.
